clue.text: Gear controls on the line?

parts.note: read as things that keep clothing (gear) held fast and under control while it hangs on a washing line

explanation.surface: A railway signalman's question about the levers that change gear on the track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gear' suggests machinery and 'the line' a railway, but gear is clothing and the line is a washing line.
explanation.definitionFit: Small wooden or plastic clips fasten laundry to a washing line so it does not blow away.

clue.text: Embellish City Road

parts.note: LA is the usual short form of Los Angeles, a city

explanation.surface: An instruction to decorate a street in town.
explanation.definitionFit: To lard a speech is to enrich or pad it out, as with fat in cooking.

clue.text: Bed-canopies checked by them?

definitions.meaning: a tester is the canopy over a four-poster bed
people who check things are inspectors or examiners

explanation.surface: Bed canopies inspected by someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Old four-poster beds carry canopies called testers; and examiners who try things out are, literally, people who test.

clue.text: Every single stunning girl, perhaps, going topless

indicators.note: losing the top letter, since in a down answer the first letter sits at the top

parts.note: a peach is slang for an attractive girl

explanation.surface: Every single attractive girl is removing her top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going topless' strips the first letter P from PEACH.
explanation.definitionFit: Each means every one taken separately, one after another.

clue.text: Monkey contained by section of low wall

indicators.note: the word for monkey is held inside the word for section

parts.note: a part is a section of something
an ape is a large monkey-like primate

explanation.surface: A monkey penned in by part of a low wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A low protective wall along the edge of a roof, bridge or balcony.

clue.text: Midnight brew that might blow up?

parts.note: the middle letter of the word night is G
ale is a brewed drink

explanation.surface: A midnight beer that could explode.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Midnight' is read as the middle of the word night, its letter G.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong wind blows up, rising suddenly in a storm.

clue.text: His tunes a shock, possibly?

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of these words may be arranged some other way

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone's music might come as a shock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges TUNES A SHOCK; the whole clue then describes the composer, whose avant-garde electronic music startled audiences.
explanation.definitionFit: Karlheinz Stockhausen was a German avant-garde composer whose electronic works shocked many listeners.

clue.text: Could have seen Garbo from a seat here

definitions.text: Could have seen Garbo from a seat here

parts.words: Could have seen Garbo from a seat here
parts.note: read as a place in a cinema or theatre balcony where one might once have watched the film star Greta Garbo

explanation.surface: A film fan recalls where they sat to watch Greta Garbo.
explanation.definitionFit: The first raised tier of seats in a theatre or cinema, once where patrons wore evening dress.

clue.text: Going soft here, they help to homes dry

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held reads 'Going soft here, they help to homes dry': a word is missing (likely 'keep' before 'homes'), and no scan or search gives the printed text.
annotationWithheld.clue: Going soft here, they help to homes dry

clue.text: Development of the novel, Greenmantle

indicators.note: novel means new, signalling the letters of the book title are made into something new

explanation.surface: How John Buchan's thriller Greenmantle came to be written.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like it describes Greenmantle, John Buchan's 1916 spy story, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: In photography, a print made larger from a negative is produced in developing film.

clue.text: Clean over sticks, these horse-races?

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece sits above the other

parts.note: to sweep is to clean with a brush
stakes are pointed wooden sticks

explanation.surface: Horses clearing jumps cleanly in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'over' puts SWEEP above STAKES.
explanation.definitionFit: A race in which all the stakes go to the winners, as in many famous flat races.

clue.text: Mole's friend is to advertise

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, used loosely here for the act of advertising; that the answer also runs through 'to advertise' is a coincidence of the charade

explanation.surface: A character from a children's book looking to promote himself.
explanation.walkthrough: Mole and Toad are friends in Kenneth Grahame's The Wind in the Willows.
explanation.definitionFit: In the classic riverbank story, the boastful amphibian of Toad Hall is Mole's companion.

clue.text: English in our time is enough for poets

parts.note: now means at the present time

explanation.surface: A claim that English today suffices for writers of verse.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for sufficient, found mainly in poetry.

clue.text: Skipper going to river for catch

parts.note: a skipper is the captain, abbreviated CAPT
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, England

explanation.surface: A boat's captain heading down to the river for a day's fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: To seize or take something prisoner, as in catching a fish or a fugitive.

clue.text: Peer in uniform

definitions.meaning: a peer is someone of the same rank or standing
uniform means the same throughout, even and level

explanation.surface: A nobleman dressed in uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: A person of matching standing; and identical in amount or degree, like an even distribution.

clue.text: Confused caterer has to go over map

indicators.note: confused means mixed up, so the letters of the word caterer are jumbled

explanation.surface: A bewildered caterer has to check a map again.
explanation.definitionFit: To trace again, going back over a route or drawing on a chart once more.

clue.text: Swift use of pawn in attack

indicators.note: the letter for the chess piece goes inside the word for attack

parts.note: a raid is a sudden attack
P is the chess abbreviation for pawn

explanation.surface: A quick chess move using a pawn in an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapid and swift both mean moving at great speed.

clue.text: Crouch down to and occupy property illegally

definitions.meaning: to sit on one's heels with knees bent
to live in an empty building without the owner's permission

explanation.surface: Someone told to hunker down and take over an empty house.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one verb: hunkering on the heels, and taking up residence in an empty building without any right.

clue.text: Poor cricket shot from captain with one hand

definitions.meaning: a stroke hitting a short ball round to leg, risky and often a way to get out
the pirate captain in Peter Pan who lost a hand to a crocodile

explanation.surface: A one-handed captain plays a bad stroke at cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A batting stroke played across the line to leg; and J. M. Barrie's villain, a pirate with a metal claw.

clue.text: Long time, it seems, in garage-sale

indicators.note: in signals that the letters lie inside the run garage-sale

explanation.surface: Waiting for ever at a car-boot style sale.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across the middle: gar-AGES-ale.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial way to describe a seemingly endless wait, as in 'I've waited for an eternity'.

clue.text: Scottish king very keen to follow daughter

indicators.note: the keen word comes after the letter for daughter

parts.note: avid means very eager

explanation.surface: An eager royal heir comes after a princess in the succession.
explanation.definitionFit: Two medieval monarchs of Scotland bore this name, David I and David II.

clue.text: Joy of French dawn

parts.note: de is French for of
first light is daybreak, so light stands for dawn

explanation.surface: The pleasure of a sunrise in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Great pleasure or happiness.

clue.text: Fellow leaves first-aid organisation to become a chronicler

indicators.note: organisation here means arrangement, so the remaining letters are reorganised
the letter for fellow departs from the letters of first-aid

explanation.surface: A man quits the ambulance service to write history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' takes F from FIRSTAID, leaving IRSTAID, which 'organisation' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who keeps a daily journal records events as they happen.

clue.text: In France, a composer to interpret

parts.note: un is French for a
Maurice Ravel was a French composer

explanation.surface: A French composer is called on to explain something.
explanation.definitionFit: To work out or solve a mystery, as one untangles knotted thread.

clue.text: Pickle in mid-meal, unusually

indicators.note: unusually signals the letters of mid-meal arranged in an odd way

explanation.surface: A pickle served unexpectedly halfway through dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pickle' looks like food, matching 'mid-meal', but means a predicament.
explanation.definitionFit: A tricky predicament, a choice between two awkward options.

clue.text: Regards affirmative voters, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly signals the word for yes voters, said aloud

parts.note: in Parliament the ayes are those voting yes

explanation.surface: A note on how those voting yes are reported.
explanation.definitionFit: To regard is to look at, watch or consider.

clue.text: Son on pitch is a celebrity

indicators.note: in a down answer the letter for son sits on top of the pitch word

parts.note: tar is black pitch

explanation.surface: A footballer's boy playing on the field becomes famous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitch' suggests a sports field but means tar.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous performer is a big name in show business.

clue.text: Tender, we hear, this King of Mercia?

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word for tender is said aloud

parts.note: to tender is to offer, as in tendering a bid

explanation.surface: A question about whether an Anglo-Saxon king was offered something.
explanation.walkthrough: Offa ruled the Anglo-Saxon kingdom of Mercia in the 8th century and built Offa's Dyke.
explanation.definitionFit: The 8th-century Anglo-Saxon ruler of the English Midlands kingdom.

clue.text: Unrepeatable opening of fairy story?

definitions.meaning: fairy tales traditionally begin with the words 'upon a time' preceded by this word

explanation.surface: The beginning of a fairy tale that cannot be told again.
explanation.definitionFit: A single occasion; and the first word of the traditional fairytale beginning.

clue.text: Where Columbus is endlessly struck, wearing spectacles?

indicators.note: the spectacles are worn around the struck word, so they enclose it

parts.note: two round lenses look like the letters OO

indicators.note: endlessly means the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: to strike is to hit, so struck gives hit

explanation.surface: Asking where the explorer Christopher Columbus, struck and bespectacled, is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Columbus' suggests the explorer, but it is the US city, capital of the state; 'endlessly' trims the final letter of the struck word before the spectacles go round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Columbus is the state capital of this US Midwestern state.

clue.text: The first gag over, is this terror eased?

definitions.text: The first gag over, is this terror eased?

parts.words: The first gag over, is this terror eased?
parts.note: read as a comedian or actor whose nerves before performing calm down once the opening joke has been delivered

explanation.surface: A comic hopes nerves settle once the opening joke lands.
explanation.definitionFit: Nervousness felt by a performer before or during an appearance before an audience.

clue.text: Extension of geometrical work

definitions.meaning: a lengthening or prolonging of something
drawing out a plan to scale with a protractor and rule, as surveyors do

explanation.surface: A deadline extension for geometry homework.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawing-out in time; and also the plotting of angles and measurements on a plan.
